Architecture and initialization

A small number of explicit owners; authored definitions, live authority, durability and presentation remain distinct.

The four layers

CaseContract
ClientInput, camera, local prediction, screens, audio and sprite presentation. Requests are not completed facts.
Zone serverLive movement validation, GAS combat, AI, resource selection/claims, fishing timing, interaction verification and current character session cache.
GameService + PostgreSQLAuthenticated identity, persistent character facts, command receipts/ledger, zone allocator/tickets, social/economy state and migrations.
Read-only contentDefinitions with stable IDs, class/ability/quest/recipe graphs, visual maps, zone/encounter/vendor/resource catalogs.

Initialization sequence

  1. Process boots and checks protocol/catalog/environment. Client local GameInstance obtains account adapter; dedicated process obtains protected service credentials.
  2. World creates GameMode/GameState and zone runtime. Resolve the ZoneDefinition and safe spawns; initialize backend adapter; reject admissions until ready.
  3. Client authenticates, selects owned CharacterId and receives a destination-bound ticket. GameMode verifies ticket/lease before possessing a gameplay pawn.
  4. Load durable snapshot and current epoch into PlayerState projection. Construct native components with explicit injected dependencies; do not depend on arbitrary component BeginPlay order.
  5. Spawn/possess Character once; bind PlayerState ASC owner and current Character avatar in Phase07. Initialize appearance/movement and ready state.
  6. On the owning client, PlayerState and possession replication may arrive in either order. A guarded readiness function creates/binds HUD once when both are ready. Immediately refresh after binding.
  7. On death/unpossession/travel, cancel actions, clear input, unbind old observers and invalidate asynchronous generation tokens. On cross-server arrival construct new framework objects from the snapshot rather than copying pointers.

Native versus Blueprint

Use shallow native ownership. ACharacter is the initial stable movement body; Paper2D visual components and one isolated PaperZD adapter provide presentation. The exact PaperZD composition API must be checked in the installed release; do not silently adopt an unverified PaperZDCharacter ancestor. Blueprint children tune capsule-safe movement values, reference definitions and assemble visuals.

Authored values use EditDefaultsOnly/BlueprintReadOnly where appropriate. Runtime state is private with read-only queries and change delegates. Exposing a setter to Blueprint does not make it network-safe; authority and ownership must be checked in native command handlers and again at durable boundaries.

One module, one backend

Begin with the RPG runtime module organized by domain folders, not a utility/manager directory full of unrelated functions. GameService is one maintainable deployable application with handlers organized by feature. PostgreSQL transactions coordinate related records. Add internal boundaries, not distributed services, when that is sufficient.

Where this plan needs proof

No installed engine/plugin was available. Public mechanisms were checked; proposed classes, request functions, replication conditions and Editor composition require implementation and two-client tests. The explicit manifest distinguishes a native role from a Blueprint child and an authored asset from runtime state.

External links need internet; the manual itself remains offline. Public documentation does not prove installed compatibility.
